251.body:
## What happened

On a developer machine, `pnpm ci:ut` fails one case, and it does so on every run, including on unmodified `main` (`9189206d`):

```text
services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts › a blocked run holds its Session queue until the user decides permission
queued work did not overtake a blocked run in the same Session
2 !== 1
```

After the failure the test process does not exit: the blocked run is cancelled only by the steps after this assertion ([L435-L453](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts#L435-L453)). The same case passes in GitHub Actions. The UT layer runs it under `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, so the run goes through JiuwenSwarm.

The second request is not the queued run. Logging the bodies that the test's fake upstream receives shows:

1. A JiuwenSwarm skill-index build, with no tools. For a full build the system prompt starts with "请为全部 Skills 构建一棵便于智能体按用户需求找到目标 Skill 的目录树…"; for an incremental one it is "You rebuild one capability-tree subtree for skill routing. Return one JSON object only."
2. The blocked run's own turn, with the run's 68 tools.

The queued run never sends a request; the queueing itself works.

## Why

1. JiuwenSwarm enables skill retrieval by default (`symphony.skill_retrieval.enabled: true` in its `jiuwenswarm/resources/config.yaml`, tag `workswarm0.2.6`). When a session starts and the instance's skill index (`<instance workspace>/symphony/skill_retrieval`) is missing or stale, Swarm starts a background index build. Its config comment says the build "uses the default configured model".
2. That default model is the adapter's `/llm/default` route, which forwards to `routes.latest()`, "the model of the run that started last and is still going" ([llm_proxy.py L109-L110](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L109-L110), [L415-L425](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L415-L425)). In this test that is the test's own run, so the build request reaches the test's fake upstream.
3. `startBlockingPermissionGateway` counts every `POST /chat/completions` as a run turn ([L125-L130](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts#L125-L130)). When the build request arrives first, it can even satisfy `waitForGatewayTurn(api, 1)`; `gatewayRunCount()` then reads 2 at the assertion.

Whether a build happens depends on the state of the JiuwenSwarm instance, not on the code under test. All rows below are on `main` `9189206d`, with `HOME` pointed at a scratch directory so that the instance is a known one:

| Instance state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh instance, this test alone | FAIL: build request first |
| Same instance again (index already built) | PASS, one request |
| Fresh instance, whole `run-cancel.test.ts` | 9/9 PASS: the file's first test, "cancelling a queued run…", triggers the build against its own upstream |
| One skill added to the instance, this test alone | FAIL: incremental rebuild request first |
| Full `pnpm ci:ut` with a fresh `HOME` | 3700/3700 PASS |

GitHub runners start each job with a fresh `HOME`, so the file's first test absorbs the build. On a developer machine the instance is `$HOME/.jiuwenswarm-instances/sd-test` (`instance_workspace` in `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`), shared by every checkout and branch that runs the layer. Branches install different skill sets into it, so its index is often stale when the test session starts.

## Expected

The test checks that the queued run does not start, whatever JiuwenSwarm does in the background:

- Count only requests that belong to the Session's runs, or assert on what the queued run did: its status, and whether any request carries its message ("This must not overtake the blocked run"). Do not assert on the total number of requests to the model endpoint.
- Cancel the blocked run in cleanup even when an assertion fails, so that a failure does not hang the worker.

Optionally, `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` gives local runs an instance that is not shared with other checkouts, or turns off the background index build for the test instance (`SYMPHONY_SKILL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED=0`).

## Related behaviour (not in scope here)

`/llm/default` sends every JiuwenSwarm-internal model call (skill-index builds, titles) to whichever run started last. With several sessions running, one session's housekeeping can be served by another session's model and credentials. The gateway already notes this ("The legacy default-model route selects the latest active endpoint, not necessarily the owner of its housekeeping work", [jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts L209-L210](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L209-L210)). It is mentioned here because it is what makes this test sensitive to instance state.
251.title: bug: run-cancel queue test counts JiuwenSwarm's own skill-index build as a second run

252.author: wyhohyw
252.body:
## What happened

The Biomni real E2E currently waits for only the first foreground Run returned by `sendUserMessage`. That Run can become `completed` after it starts a managed background shell Execution. When the Execution finishes, the product delivers its result to the main Agent in a later automatic wake Run. The E2E may check final artifacts and clean up the Session before that wake Run finishes, reporting an incomplete delivery as a failure.

This was observed during local Biomni DA-13-3 and DA-14-1 investigations: the first Run's terminal status was not a reliable signal that the entire request had produced its final answer. The fix is limited to the test harness; the product's separate Run and Execution lifecycles are intentional.

## Expected

- Follow the initial Run, main-Agent background Executions, and subsequent automatic main-Agent wake Runs before asserting final delivery.
- Ignore unrelated subagent Executions and wakes when deciding whether the main request is complete.
- After all observed work is terminal, use a short quiet window to catch a wake Run created just after an Execution finishes.
- On budget expiry, distinguish timeout from a completed run with missing artifacts and cancel active Runs in the Session.
- Cover the settling rules with deterministic unit tests. Keep the existing manual Biomni entry point and quarantine unchanged.

Related: #233 concerns the missing error text in a delivery assertion; this issue concerns checking delivery before the complete Run chain finishes.
252.title: bug(e2e): Biomni delivery is checked before automatic wake Runs finish

257.author: zhaozhaozz
257.body:
ScienceDiscovery should keep its JiuwenSwarm runtime data under the user's home directory while using a namespace separate from a standalone JiuwenSwarm installation. Today, normal local startup shares the instance registry, and an existing instance with the same name can be reused unintentionally.

## Current behavior

Without directory overrides, the pinned JiuwenSwarm version (`workswarm0.2.6`) uses:

| Consumer | Runtime workspace |
| --- | --- |
| Standalone JiuwenSwarm, unnamed instance | `~/.jiuwenswarm/` |
| Standalone named instance | `~/.jiuwenswarm-instances/<name>/` |
| ScienceDiscovery's default named instance | `~/.jiuwenswarm-instances/sciencediscovery/` |

Named instances share `~/.jiuwenswarm/instances.yaml`. Separate instance names keep their workspaces apart, but they do not isolate the registry.

`scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh` defaults `JIUWENSWARM_INSTANCE` to `sciencediscovery`. Its setup path skips instance creation when the workspace already exists, then calls `apply_config()` on that workspace. This can change a user's independently created instance, including `progressive_tool_enabled` and the default search switches. Start/stop operations also address that same instance.

The install location (`JIUWENSWARM_ROOT` / `JIUWENSWARM_SRC`) is separate from the runtime namespace; changing the install location alone does not fix this collision.

## Reproduction outline

Use a disposable home namespace supported by `JIUWENSWARM_HOME`; do not run this against personal data.

1. Initialize a standalone JiuwenSwarm named instance `sciencediscovery` in that namespace and record its configuration.
2. Configure the ScienceDiscovery wrapper to use the same namespace and leave its instance name at the default.
3. Run the wrapper's setup command.
4. Observe that it reuses the existing workspace and adjusts its configuration instead of creating a separate ScienceDiscovery-owned workspace.

This is established from the setup/path-resolution code. No personal home directory was modified to reproduce it.

## Expected behavior and proposed direction

- Preserve home-based defaults for ordinary user startup.
- Give the embedded backend a ScienceDiscovery-specific root, for example `JIUWENSWARM_HOME=$HOME/.sciencediscovery/jiuwenswarm`, with its own registry and named instance workspaces beneath it.
- Keep explicit directory overrides supported. Test runners must continue using their own per-run directories without changing the process `HOME`.
- Resolve setup/start/status/env/stop and runtime logs against the same root. Reuse the pinned installation independently of runtime state.
- Define migration for existing ScienceDiscovery instances before changing the default. Do not automatically move, rewrite, or delete an ambiguous standalone instance merely because its name is `sciencediscovery`.
- Preserve Docker's persisted-volume behavior and document the resulting local/container paths.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Standalone JiuwenSwarm and ScienceDiscovery can both use an instance named `sciencediscovery` without sharing registry, configuration, or session data.
2. Setting up, starting, or stopping either application does not modify or stop the other application's instance; port allocation must also allow coexistence.
3. Normal local startup stores runtime data under the user's home by default; explicit overrides and isolated test runs still work.
4. Existing ScienceDiscovery users have a documented migration or compatibility path that protects standalone data.

This issue covers normal product startup. The test-runtime isolation work in #259 (part of #248) is separate and does not change the ordinary user default.
257.title: [Bug]: Isolate embedded JiuwenSwarm data from standalone user instances

260.author: zhaozhaozz
260.body:
## What happened

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is a test-only variable. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1` whenever the backend is JiuwenSwarm, together with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=task`. Twelve specs then gate on it: `expect(process.env.E2E_SWARM_TASK !== "1", "BLOCKED: …").toBe(false)`. No product code reads it.

The precondition it stands for is real: these journeys exercise sub-agents delegated through the platform `task` tool (sandbox, deliverables, sub-agent cards), and some of them exercise JiuwenSwarm itself. As a switch, though, it does not do that job:

- It is a declaration, not a check. A stack started with `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=jiuwenswarm`, the one configuration where the precondition fails, still passes if someone exports `E2E_SWARM_TASK=1`.
- In CI it is always `1` on the default backend, so it never stops anything there.
- It blocks journeys that do not depend on JiuwenSwarm. The built-in (native) loop also delegates through the platform `task` tool, but DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on it unless the variable is set by hand.
- Anyone running a real journey by hand has to remember it; three benchmark READMEs say so.
- `deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` and `biomnibench-da-swarm.spec.ts` write `backend: "jiuwenswarm"` into their score metrics as a constant, so a native run is labelled as JiuwenSwarm.

## Proposal

- `/health` (and `/api/health`) reports how the stack runs agent turns, from the API's own configuration: `agent: { executor: "jiuwenswarm" | "native", subagents: "task" | "jiuwenswarm" }`. The native loop always delegates through `task`. The API is the component that makes this decision in both modes; the adapter's `/agent/info` does not exist when the stack runs natively.
- One E2E helper reads it. Real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require platform `task` delegation on either executor. Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour (`swarm-*`, `literature-review-*`, `artifact-revision`) also require the `jiuwenswarm` executor. A mismatch is reported as BLOCKED with what the stack actually reported.
- `E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `run-e2e.sh`, the specs and the READMEs.
- Score metrics record the executor the stack reported, not a constant.
- `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE`, `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION`, `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY` stay. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

262.author: wyhohyw
262.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [ ] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

### Summary

When a subagent emits several independent biomedical MCP tool calls in one model response, ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler` executes them one at a time. The workspace registers opaque MCP tools without an `isConcurrencySafe` classifier, so the registry marks them `exclusive` even when JiuwenSwarm submits the requests concurrently. This adds avoidable latency to read-only literature searches. See the 2026-10-12 root-cause comment below for the stage trace and evidence boundary.

### Reproduction

1. Configure a public biomedical MCP source such as PubMed, allowing at least two concurrent source requests.
2. Have a ScienceDiscovery `task` subagent request six independent PubMed MCP searches in one model turn. Test both `allow` and `ask` (approve all six for the latter).
3. Compare the model batch, JiuwenSwarm/MCP SDK request starts, ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` classification, and broker start/end timestamps.

### Observed

In a DA-13-3 local E2E trace, one model SSE summary reported `toolCalls: 6` and `finishReason: tool_calls`. The six approvals were posted close together, but each MCP search started only after the previous search finished. Across the full subagent trace, 49 literature MCP invocations (42 PubMed, 7 Europe PMC) had **zero pairwise execution overlap**; their individual durations summed to 166.6 s. Broker `queueWaitMs` was 0, so its rate/concurrency queue does not explain the serialization. A representative six-call batch took 14.59 s wall time for 12.13 s summed tool execution.

A different DA-13-3 no-subagent trace shows that the main agent's built-in calls can overlap: six `free_search` calls summed to 88.6 s but occupied 21.9 s of union wall time; 24 `fetch_webpage` calls summed to 42.1 s but occupied 15.3 s. These are different tools and workloads, so this is evidence that overlap is possible, **not** a direct speed comparison.

### Expected

Independent read-only calls explicitly classified as concurrency-safe should run concurrently within the source's configured limits. Under `ask`, each call must still receive its own authorization decision; denied calls remain denied.

### Confirmed serialization path

- `packages/workspace/src/workspace.ts` `createMcpTools` does not declare `isConcurrencySafe` for opaque MCP tools. The existing workspace test explicitly checks this default.
- `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` `executionMode` returns `exclusive` when that classifier is absent.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` `ToolScheduler.run` waits for earlier same-batch calls whenever their execution mode is not `parallel`, before the call reaches the broker.
- Stage instrumentation confirmed that six PubMed calls overlap at the JiuwenSwarm tool and MCP SDK request entries under `allow`, while their broker intervals remain serial. The `ask` resume path adds latency but does not cause the common serialization.

### Measured scheduler control and performance boundary

**Product-path dispatch:** In the controlled six-PubMed-call `allow` probes, the original broker calls started one after another. With the read-only concurrency opt-in, all six began within 44 ms and the source broker then applied its own queue/concurrency limits. The batches took 12.09 s and 7.22 s respectively, but their successful-result counts differed (2/6 versus 1/6); those wall times are **not** a clean successful-workload speed comparison.

**Network-free scheduler control:** A fake JiuwenSwarm adapter submitted the same six fixed-success, MCP-like calls in one model response. Each call took 150 ms; a local two-permit limiter simulated the PubMed source concurrency ceiling. Across five repetitions per mode, every call succeeded:

| Classification | Six-call batch span, five runs | Median | Max active |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exclusive | 921.2–925.6 ms | 923.4 ms | 1 |
| Parallel-safe | 451.5–454.4 ms | 452.6 ms | 2 |

This measures about a 51% shorter batch span in ScienceDiscovery's `ToolScheduler`, with the simulated source limit intact. It does not include the real MCP broker, model, or provider. The temporary diagnostic test was removed after running.

**Real-provider support outside ScienceDiscovery:** A separate no-model harness requested the same six public PubMed topics, including eSearch and eSummary, with at most two search jobs and at most two HTTP requests per second. In serial/parallel/parallel/serial order, the batch results were 10.031 s (6/6), 6.797 s (5/6; one HTTP 429), 6.344 s (6/6), and 11.359 s (6/6). The fully successful parallel block was quicker than either fully successful serial block. This supports the scheduling direction but is **not** a product E2E before/after or evidence of a success-rate improvement. [Methods and per-run data](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/262#issuecomment-6119154713).

**Whole-run boundary:** In the earlier DA-13-3 trace, 49 literature MCP calls occupied 189.6 s across ten contiguous batches. An optimistic two-concurrent-per-source schedule estimates 89.2 s, or about **100.4 s potential saving**; that remains a scheduling estimate, not a measured whole-run improvement. The 962.5 s E2E also includes different research work and model turns. A stable-provider, same-workload MCP integration benchmark is still needed before claiming an end-to-end speedup.

### Suggested acceptance test

Classify only known read-only MCP operations as parallel-safe; keep opaque/mutating tools exclusive. Use six independent read-only MCP calls emitted in one model turn under both `allow` and `ask`. Assert broker execution intervals overlap while respecting per-source concurrency/rate limits. Also cover mixed allow/deny decisions, preapproved calls, and correct replay after interruption.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Observed in local ScienceDiscovery E2E checkouts on 2026-10-09 (Windows host + WSL Linux runtime, x86_64).
- ScienceDiscovery API/adapter with installed JiuwenSwarm/OpenJiuwen runtime; public PubMed and Europe PMC MCP tools.
- PubMed source governance allowed up to two concurrent requests and three requests per second; broker reported `queueWaitMs: 0` for the observed calls.
- The model provider is not needed for reproduction: a deterministic model stub that emits one batch of six independent MCP `tool_calls` would isolate this behavior.
- No private API key or raw trace is attached.

### Additional Information

Related: #230 documents a separate CAS commit-validation bottleneck. The MCP serialization here remains observable with that optimization applied and also under `allow`. The 100.4 s figure above remains a bounded estimate; the new scheduler and provider controls do not replace a same-workload MCP integration benchmark.

### Version Information

Observed on the 2026-10-09 ScienceDiscovery experimental E2E checkout based on commit `4ece4d3` plus the local CAS commit-validation experiment discussed in #230. The 2026-10-12 controlled probe used a separate isolated checkout based on `4cf846f`; installed runtime metadata reported `openjiuwen 0.1.17` and editable `workswarm 0.2.5b1`. This report identifies the ScienceDiscovery `ToolScheduler` policy in the tested checkout; it does not claim that every MCP operation is safe to run concurrently.

263.author: zhaozhaozz
263.body:
## What happened

Nightly trial run [38107013490](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38107013490) (real model, built-in agent loop) was cancelled by hand during its fourth journey. By then three of its ten journeys had already failed: DRB-59, DRB-64 and DRB-58, each after 83–90 minutes. Nothing that was uploaded says why:

- The job log (and `run.log`) has one `✘` line per journey, and no error.
- Each journey report says **FAIL** with "0 / 0 steps passed", and no error.
- `test-results/` is missing. That is where `benchmark-metrics.json` (run status, delivery, error, sub-agents), `error-context.md` and the trace would be. `summary.txt` is missing too.

What could be reconstructed from `stack.log` timing alone: DRB-58 used up its 90-minute run budget. DRB-59 and DRB-64 ended on their own after 83–84 minutes, well inside their 120-minute budget, and then failed at the delivery assertion. Whether those two runs failed, or completed without a readable report, can no longer be told.

## Why

1. **Per-test evidence is copied only on exit.** Playwright writes `test-results/` to `.e2e/test-results`, which is outside the uploaded results directory. `.ci/run-e2e.sh` copies it there only in its EXIT trap. When a job is cancelled, the runner sends SIGINT, then SIGTERM about 7.5 s later, then kills the process tree about 2.5 s after that. bash runs the trap only once Playwright has exited, and Playwright was still tearing down the running journey: its `finally` alone waits up to 30 s for the run to cancel. So the copy never happens. A job timeout or a lost runner has the same effect.
2. **The `list` reporter prints failure details only when the whole run ends.** As each test ends, it prints just the `✘` line.
3. **Journey reports only record errors raised inside `journey.step()`.** The reports themselves are written into the results as each journey ends, which is why they survived. But the benchmark journeys assert in the test body, so their reports carry no error at all.

## Expected

Every journey that has finished leaves its evidence in the uploaded results at the moment it finishes. Its failure reason can be read in the job log and in its journey report without waiting for the rest of the run, whether or not the run ends normally.

## Proposal

- `run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`, and `test/playwright.config.ts` uses it as `outputDir` (falling back to `.e2e/test-results`). The exit trap then copies only the HTML report, which Playwright renders once the run ends anyway.
- A journey report that failed without a failed step gets a "failure reason" section from `testInfo.errors`. It is redacted and truncated like step errors already are.
- When a journey fails, print the first lines of its error after its `journey report (FAIL)` line: the assertion message and expected/received, without the stack, and redacted.

Not in scope: for a cancelled layer, the shared-plan summary still reports "no frozen plan reported … the layer stopped before it collected its tests", because the shared runner writes its accounting only after Playwright exits. With the evidence above, a cancelled run can be diagnosed regardless.

Related: #233 (a delivery failure does not carry the run's own error).
263.title: bug(e2e): A cancelled or killed E2E run loses the failure evidence of journeys that already finished

264.author: zy95-12
264.body:
## Background and environment

During a source installation on a Debian 13 cloud desktop on 2026-10-11, using main commit `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, two problems required manual investigation:

1. The desktop terminal did not inherit the outbound proxy environment. The initial managed micromamba download failed with `ECONNREFUSED`; an installation environment with the required network configuration could complete the download.
2. When the adapter inherited a SOCKS proxy configuration, it failed to start because `socksio` was missing, affecting access to the application.

The first observation is an environment-triggered failure, not proof of a downloader implementation defect. The second has a concrete dependency declaration gap.

## Conditions and observed behavior

### A. Different proxy environments across installation and runtime entry points

- External access required a proxy, but the terminal initiating scientific-environment preparation did not inherit the corresponding configuration.
- The micromamba connection was refused and scientific-environment preparation could not complete.
- Installation succeeded through an official download/install path with the necessary network configuration, retaining the pinned version and SHA-256 verification.
- The scientific environment subsequently became ready, with Python 3.12, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib available.

### B. SOCKS configuration prevents adapter startup

- Create a clean adapter environment from the declared project dependencies and start it with a valid SOCKS proxy configuration.
- During HTTP client initialization, the missing socksio dependency prevents adapter startup.
- In this installation, adding socksio from official PyPI to the adapter's isolated environment restored startup; API health and page HTML checks then passed.

Source references:
- [Adapter declares plain httpx](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/pyproject.toml#L19-L25).
- [HTTP clients are constructed during startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/app.py#L47-L63).

## User impact

- Users may have already installed the source and other dependencies, yet still be blocked at first startup or scientific-environment preparation, preventing access to the workbench or relevant computations.
- Users must investigate differences between terminal and child-process proxy environments, and may need to install undeclared dependencies manually.
- A component-level failure can look like a failed installation of the entire application, leading to unnecessary reinstalls. This is not evidence that micromamba itself is unsuitable or unavailable.

## Expected behavior and proposed improvements

1. Unify installation/startup preflight checks: inspect the actual child process's proxy configuration, connectivity to required download sources, and dependencies for the selected proxy protocol. Report redacted status, never credentials.
2. Declare and lock SOCKS support, for example through `httpx[socks]`. Define the proxy boundary between loopback service calls and external requests, including correct `NO_PROXY` handling.
3. Identify the failing component, stage, underlying cause, and actionable next step. After configuration is corrected, allow retrying the failed step while reusing verified tools and caches.
4. Report Web entry point, adapter, and scientific-environment readiness separately instead of treating partial readiness as an all-or-nothing result.

The repository already has [download retry and cache mechanisms](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/fetch-managed-micromamba.mjs#L179-L295), as well as [classified errors and mirror/preinstalled-tool recovery guidance](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/environment-store.ts#L1138-L1173). The goal is to connect these capabilities into a coherent first-run experience, not to replace the downloader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean adapter environment starts with HTTP/SOCKS proxy configurations without manually installing undeclared dependencies.
- [ ] Missing or incorrect proxy configuration produces redacted, actionable diagnostics while retaining the underlying error.
- [ ] Correcting configuration allows retrying the failed step and reusing verified artifacts, without clearing all data or reinstalling.
- [ ] Version pinning and hash verification remain enforced; recovery does not disable TLS verification.
- [ ] Tests cover no proxy, HTTP/SOCKS proxies, unreachable download sources, and successful retry after correction; installation documentation is updated.

Related: #29 (actionable dependency preflight), #213 and #229 (onboarding feedback). This issue focuses on the observed proxy-related failures and first-install recovery experience.
264.title: [Bug]: Improve proxy-aware installation: declare SOCKS support and unify preflight and recovery

265.author: zy95-12
265.body:
## Problem and goal

Containers, restricted cloud environments, and remote compute nodes may have bubblewrap installed but prohibit the namespaces or mounts it needs. The ability to install, build, and open the workbench should be separate from the selected Runner's ability to execute code safely.

Users should not need to understand execution modes before using the product. Installation and builds should not be blocked by execution-mode requirements. Explain the limitation and offer choices only when a task actually needs code execution and the selected Runner cannot satisfy its requirements.

## Observed environments and results

On 2026-10-11, different execution environments produced different results. These observations do **not** support a blanket claim that cloud desktops cannot run sandboxes:

1. **Restricted cloud coding container:** while investigating main `cc95884428e64ae853d8758574fff5107c6347f0`, bubblewrap failed with `setting up uid map: Read-only file system`, consistent with that environment's /proc restrictions. Source installation and builds could complete, but sandbox execution remained unavailable.
2. **Tool execution session on another cloud desktop:** at main `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`, the project's sandbox probe failed with `loopback: Failed to create NETLINK_ROUTE socket: Operation not permitted`.
3. **Desktop terminal on that same cloud desktop:** the same probe succeeded, and the Runner and workbench subsequently started from the desktop terminal. No sandbox disabling or host security-policy changes were required. The tool session and desktop terminal occupied different network namespaces.

Capability checks must therefore run in the **actual execution environment of the selected Runner**. A failure in an installation shell or another session must not be generalized to the entire machine. Likewise, a remote node merely appearing to be containerized does not establish adequate isolation.

## Current implementation and consequences

Code observations below refer to `5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08`:

- Standalone dependency installation and builds are possible, but the [one-command source startup path](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L326-L395) checks sandbox executables before installation/build. It also [waits for Runner health before proceeding with API/UI startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/scripts/start-stack.sh#L626). Missing sandbox dependencies or a Runner startup failure can therefore prevent access to the workbench.
- [Runner startup preflight](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/server.ts#L1086-L1142) handles failures differently: some Linux sandbox failures only produce a warning, whereas missing/incompatible executables or unusable Seatbelt prevent startup. Process liveness or HTTP health is not equivalent to code-execution readiness.
- Internal probes already expose information such as sandboxUsable, but this is not yet an end-to-end capability and recovery contract spanning Runner registration, task dispatch, and the UI.
- [Code tool bindings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/agent-run/workspace-bindings.ts#L174-L219) do not provide a dedicated just-in-time choice flow for unavailable sandbox execution. Generic permission to run code is not consent to unsandboxed execution.
- [Ordinary code execution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/runner/src/executor.ts#L933-L1003) still depends on bubblewrap/Seatbelt; there is no general-purpose unsandboxed backend. The direct connection setting means a direct connection to a Runner, not unsandboxed execution.
- The [existing permission mechanism](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/5ddaa38bd68a84e4e20b14116d91880fe87bdd08/services/api/src/permissions/index.ts#L28-L80) may provide an interaction foundation, but it does not establish that execution-mode switching, dedicated consent, and reliable recovery already exist.

User impact:
1. Users who only want to install, build, configure models, or browse the workbench may be blocked by local compute prerequisites.
2. A service may appear connected, yet fail when code is executed, making sandbox, network, dependency, and model failures difficult to distinguish.
3. Users with an available remote Runner may still have to troubleshoot local execution; restricted-environment users lack an actionable in-product next step.
4. Silently falling back to direct execution would remove isolation without informed consent, increasing exposure of files, processes, and credentials.

## Expected behavior

1. **Decouple installation, builds, and workbench startup from execution readiness.** Allow installation/build and non-execution configuration/browsing when the local Runner is unavailable. Clearly indicate compute limitations rather than claiming full readiness.
2. **Probe capabilities per Runner.** Distinguish connectivity, dependencies, sandbox availability, and execution readiness; retain structured failure reasons and validate them at the actual execution location.
3. **Ask only when execution requires a decision.** Use an available safe execution path by default. When blocked, explain why and offer an available Runner, environment repair, or cancellation. Do not force users to choose modes during installation.
4. **If direct-execution fallback is supported, design it explicitly.** Reuse task orchestration and artifact handling, branching at the execution backend. Never silently downgrade. Explain the affected scope and obtain dedicated consent first; authorization scope, lifetime, and invalidation require design review.
5. **Retain product responsibility for safety.** An assertion that the external environment is controlled must not replace validation, hazardous-action controls, auditing, cancellation, or recovery. This issue does not request disabling host security policies or bypassing platform restrictions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Independent installation/build completes in three cases: bwrap missing, bwrap present but namespace creation denied, and a working sandbox.
- [ ] When local compute is unavailable, the workbench supports permitted non-execution flows and clearly reports limited capabilities.
- [ ] Preflight results belong to the selected Runner's actual execution environment, not another shell or node.
- [ ] A task requiring code execution reports the blocking reason and allows an available Runner or cancellation; normal environments do not gain unnecessary prompts.
- [ ] If direct execution is implemented, it requires consent distinct from generic code permission, has no silent fallback, and produces auditable records.
- [ ] Tests cover rejection/cancellation, repeated execution, Runner changes, capability changes, and process restarts; already completed side effects must not be duplicated.

## Related issues and scope

- #38 covers the mismatch between serve readiness and actual compute readiness. This issue additionally covers installation/startup decoupling, actual-Runner capability probes, just-in-time interaction, and fallback design.
- #29 covers actionable dependency preflight guidance.
- #264 separately tracks proxy, micromamba download, and SOCKS dependency installation usability.
- These are requirements and design proposals, not a claim that an unsandboxed backend already exists. Delivery staging and the precise direct-execution authorization contract remain design decisions.
265.title: [Feature]: Decouple sandbox readiness from installation and workbench startup; offer choices when execution is blocked

267.author: zhaozhaozz
267.body:
## Context

`GET /health` and `GET /api/health` on the API are answered before authentication: they are the first route in the request handler in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`. That is deliberate. Container health checks call the endpoint without a token: the `Dockerfile` `HEALTHCHECK` and the `docker-compose.yml` healthcheck both run `curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:4310/health`. The Runner's own `GET /health` is unauthenticated as well. `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts` relies on that being known: when it connects to a direct Runner, it checks the token against an authenticated endpoint instead.

The question came up in the review of #261, which adds `agent: { executor, subagents }` to the API's `/health`. That field matters little next to what the endpoint already returns, so this issue is about the endpoint as a whole.

## What an unauthenticated caller receives today

From the API's `/health`:

- `sandboxNetwork`: the administrator's sandbox network settings, including `allowedDomains` and `allowPrivateNetwork`, plus the Runner's network capability.
- `runner`: the Runner's whole health record, passed through as-is. That includes `executionUser`, `platform`, `runnerVersion`, `sandbox`, `seccompBaseline`, `executionTimeoutMs`, the output and workspace limits, and the scientific-environment and NPU capabilities.
- `workspace`: the upload and workspace quotas.
- `memoryGraph` status and `milestone`; with #261, also `agent`.

The Runner's `/health` returns the same Runner record directly.

## Exposure

By default the API and the Runner both bind `127.0.0.1`, and Docker Compose publishes on `127.0.0.1`, so a default install shows this only to the local machine. The endpoint reaches the network in two cases:

- A user sets `SCIENCE_AGENT_PUBLISH_HOST=0.0.0.0` to open the UI to other machines.
- A user starts a Runner on another machine for remote execution, which has to listen on a reachable address.

An unauthenticated caller then learns the sandbox egress allowlist, whether the sandbox may reach private networks, the user commands run as, and the exact Runner version. None of that is a credential or user data, but it is the reconnaissance an attacker of the sandbox would want first.

## Proposal

- Keep `/health` public, but reduce the unauthenticated response to liveness: `service` and `status` for the API, `status` for the Runner. That is all the container health checks read.
- Return the detail only to a caller that presents a valid token, either on the same route or on a separate authenticated one. The web client already sends its bearer token on every request, including both of its `/health` reads (memory-graph status and workspace limits). The E2E helpers `requireRealStack()` and `requireAgentStack()` would send `E2E_API_TOKEN`.
- Stop the API from passing the Runner's full record through any unauthenticated response.
- Add tests asserting that an unauthenticated `/health` on either service exposes nothing beyond liveness, and that the health checks still pass.

Not in scope: what the authenticated health record contains.
267.title: security(api): Unauthenticated /health returns deployment details, not just liveness

276.body:
## Summary

Allow an Agent, with explicit user authorization, to execute commands and scientific code directly on a local or remote machine when sandbox execution is unavailable. Keep the decision and recovery flow in the conversation, and preserve execution traces and artifact provenance.

This is a follow-up to #265 and PR #275, **not a requirement blocking their closure**. #275 addresses readiness, actionable failures and Agent-controlled waiting; it deliberately does not implement unsandboxed execution.

## Problem

A connected Runner may be unable to create the sandbox because of missing dependencies or namespace restrictions. Today the user can repair the environment, switch Runner, or cancel, but cannot explicitly authorize direct execution on an otherwise usable machine. This blocks both environment maintenance and scientific computation in restricted environments.

A generic permission to run sandboxed code is not consent to expose the host's files, processes, network and credentials. Direct execution must therefore be an explicit, governed execution path, never a silent retry after sandbox failure.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Conversation-first consent.** When blocked, the Agent may propose direct execution, explaining the target machine, execution identity, command/purpose, working directory and loss of sandbox isolation. The user can authorize or decline without first visiting Settings. Do not introduce a mandatory extra global toggle merely for this interaction.
2. **Explicit authorization scope.** Extend the existing permission framework with an execution-mode/target scope. Support a clearly bounded one-operation authorization first; discuss optional reusable grants, expiry and revocation. Existing sandbox-oriented Always Allow settings must not silently authorize host execution. Child Agents may only inherit explicitly granted scope.
3. **Local and remote execution.** Reuse the current task/executor flow and select the direct backend at the execution boundary. Operate only with the configured OS account's privileges; do not implicitly elevate to root or change host security policy. A Runner's direct HTTP connection is not the same as unsandboxed execution.
4. **Actual reachability and recovery.** Probe the selected target's direct-execution capability separately from sandbox readiness. If the remote Runner is unreachable, remote maintenance requires an independently configured and authorized connection such as SSH; do not assume one exists. Initially, a reachable Runner's direct backend may be delivered separately from this maintenance transport.
5. **Keep lifecycle and audit guarantees.** Retain progress/output, timeout, cancellation and artifact handling. Record target, execution mode, user/account, authorization reference, command, timestamps and outcome with the run/agent/tool-call identity. Explain that unsandboxed host-side effects cannot all be confined to the workspace or rolled back; existing workspace artifact tracking is not comprehensive host auditing.
6. **No duplicate or implicit replay.** Returning a decision to the Agent must not automatically replay the blocked command. The Agent confirms the target/workspace and submits a new authorized execution. If dispatch outcome is unknown, reconcile it rather than blindly retrying side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With sandbox unavailable but target reachable, an explicitly approved harmless shell/Python operation can execute locally and on a configured remote target.
- [ ] Without direct-execution consent, execution remains blocked; refusal/cancellation produces no host command or silent fallback.
- [ ] Authorization cannot leak across targets, execution identities or child Agents; reusable grants have defined expiry/revocation semantics.
- [ ] Progress, cancellation, timeout and final errors remain visible in the conversation; the execution mode and authorization are auditable alongside resulting workspace artifacts.
- [ ] Tests cover sandbox failure, consent/deny, scope changes, remote disconnect, uncertain execution outcome and cancellation without duplicate side effects.

## Design questions

Define the minimum authorization scope/lifetime, whether direct execution is also available by explicit request before sandbox failure, and the first-version boundary for SSH maintenance. Any unavailable resource/network isolation or process-tree cancellation guarantees must be documented rather than presented as equivalent to sandbox execution.

Out of scope: silently disabling isolation, bypassing OS/platform restrictions, provisioning credentials, or automatically granting administrative privileges.
276.title: [Feature]: Authorize direct execution on local and remote machines when sandbox execution is unavailable

278.author: wyhohyw
278.body:
## Problem

ScienceDiscovery exposes many settings, but a user working in a conversation often does not know which page or field will unblock the current task. For example, adding a model API can require entering a service URL/key, registering a model, selecting its scope, and returning to the original request. A settings-page wizard for initial model connection was proposed in #39; this issue covers **configuration discovered during a task and completed inside the conversation**.

## Proposed experience

Keep existing valid settings and defaults. When a concrete task is blocked by a supported missing capability, or the user explicitly asks for a change:

1. The Agent explains the need in the context of the task and proposes **one specific change**. It pre-fills facts it knows and asks only for missing fields.
2. An in-conversation card shows the current → proposed value, where a resource will be saved, where it will be used (session/project/global), the target service or file, and any connection test or other external action.
3. The user fills in any remaining URL, credential, supported path, or selection and clicks **“Confirm configuration and continue”** (or declines). This one action confirms the fully visible change and the continuation intent.
4. A trusted configuration service validates, tests as disclosed, applies, and then resumes the task. A validation error remains on the card for correction. The result separately reports **saved**, **effective for the task**, and **task resumed/queued**.

For example: “This image analysis needs a vision-capable model. Add this supported model service with its API URL and key, test the selected model, save the provider in this deployment, and use the model in this session.” If an existing vision model is available, offer a one-click session selection instead.

The normal settings pages remain available for inspection and manual management. A usable default should never trigger a configuration interruption merely because another option might be better.

## V1 scope

- Select an already configured model for the current session.
- Add a model connection through an **already supported provider/protocol**, provide or repair its credential, verify it, and bind a selected model to the session. Creating a provider resource does **not** silently change the global default.
- Enable an installed, already configured connector for the session. Its later tool calls still follow the existing execution-permission rules.
- Show the same card without relying on the Agent when no model is configured or the current model's authentication has failed; preserve the user's first task and start it once configuration succeeds.
- Persist card state across refresh/reconnect and continue through a linked follow-up run when the active run's model/tool snapshot must change.

A URL alone must not be treated as a usable arbitrary REST tool. New HTTP/SSE MCP connections, OAuth, controlled file/environment imports, and deployment-wide proxy/timeout changes can follow with dedicated adapters. STDIO commands, host execution, restart-required deployment settings, and arbitrary REST adaptation need separate review.

## Design constraints

- The Agent may inspect a **redacted** capability catalog and create a structured proposal. Only a user-bound decision endpoint may approve it; the Agent must not receive a generic settings-write tool or claim user consent through another tool.
- Secrets use dedicated fields and encrypted backend storage. Plaintext keys must not enter chat messages, model context, tool traces, SSE events, ordinary logs, or browser persistence. A local browser path is not a server path; any supported file import must show the exact environment and read scope.
- Show the real save scope and effective-use scope. Prefer a session override when supported; disclose shared-resource or global effects before confirmation. Do not invent a session-only option for a system-wide setting.
- Bind approval to a proposal revision and concrete target, diff, scope, and verification plan. Re-preview after concurrent setting changes. External probes or reads require explicit disclosure; failed validation must leave the effective configuration intact.
- Do not hot-swap an in-flight run's snapshot by assumption. Finish or stop at a safe boundary, account for pending tools and side effects, then create an idempotent linked continuation using the approved new snapshot. Stop/cancel must suppress automatic continuation. Saved configuration and resumed execution are distinct states.
- An undo action should preview the reverse change and use version checks; it must not overwrite later edits or delete a shared resource still in use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing valid configuration remains unchanged and completes a task without a card.
- [ ] A supported missing model API can be entered, confirmed, verified, saved, and used to continue from the conversation, without visiting settings.
- [ ] Selecting an existing vision model changes only the intended scope; other sessions and global defaults remain unchanged.
- [ ] Invalid credentials do not replace the current working connection; a corrected submission applies once. Supported keyless local endpoints also work.
- [ ] No-model and authentication-failure entry points work without asking a broken model to diagnose itself.
- [ ] Plaintext secrets never appear in messages, events, logs, tool history, or model requests; Agent calls cannot approve a proposal.
- [ ] The displayed resource location, effective scope, target, and possible verification cost match what the backend actually does.
- [ ] Decline/cancel does not repeatedly re-prompt for the same need; a blocked task has a clear reason and any viable alternative.
- [ ] Double-clicks, refresh, SSE replay, retries, and restart recovery create at most one configuration application and one continuation run.
- [ ] Concurrent settings edits make the old proposal stale instead of overwriting the newer value.
- [ ] The old run keeps its historical snapshot; the linked continuation uses the approved new snapshot, preserves the goal and completed artifacts, and does not replay non-idempotent actions.
- [ ] Validation, save, and continuation failures have separate truthful states and phase-specific recovery.
- [ ] Stop, session switching, archival, and deletion cannot apply a proposal in the wrong session or restart a stopped task.
- [ ] Undo restores the former override/inheritance relationship without clobbering subsequent changes or removing a resource used elsewhere.
- [ ] The card supports keyboard use, accessible errors, narrow screens, and Chinese/English text.

## Relation to existing work

#39 addresses a first-connection wizard in settings; this proposal adds task-contextual, Agent-assisted configuration and continuation. The current mainline backend work in #84 (including models/settings #91, chat/runs #89, and MCP #92) should determine the final service and event integration. The product behavior above is the contract; implementation paths and API shapes from the local design draft should be reconciled with current main before coding.

## 中文版

### 问题

ScienceDiscovery 有不少设置。用户正在对话里完成任务时，往往不知道哪个页面、哪个字段能够解决眼前的问题。例如接入模型 API，可能要填写服务地址和密钥、注册模型、选择作用范围，再回到原任务。#39 提出的是设置页中的首次模型接入向导；本 Issue 关注的是**任务进行中发现配置缺口，并在对话内完成配置**。

### 期望交互

默认沿用已有的有效配置。只有当前任务确实缺少受支持的能力，或用户主动要求修改时，才进入以下流程：

1. Agent 结合当前任务说明原因，提出**一项明确变更**。已知信息预填，只询问缺少的字段。
2. 对话卡片展示当前值 → 建议值、资源保存位置、实际使用范围（会话／项目／全局）、目标服务或文件，以及即将执行的连接测试等外部动作。
3. 用户补齐必要的地址、凭据、受支持的路径或选择后，点击「确认配置并继续」；也可以拒绝。这一次提交确认的是卡片中完整可见的变更和接续意图。
4. 可信配置服务按卡片说明校验、测试、应用配置，再接续任务。验证失败留在原卡片修正。结果分别说明**配置已保存**、**对任务已生效**、**任务已开始接续或进入队列**，不把三者混为一谈。

例如：「本次图片分析需要支持视觉的模型。请提供受支持的模型服务地址和 API Key；我会测试所选模型，在本部署保存服务，并仅将该模型用于当前会话。」如果已有可用视觉模型，应优先给出一次确认即可完成的会话级选择。

设置页继续作为集中查看和手动维护入口。只要默认配置能完成任务，就不应仅因为存在“更优”选项而打断用户。

### 首版范围

- 为当前会话选择已配置的模型。
- 通过**已有支持的提供方／协议**添加模型连接，补充或修复凭据，验证后把所选模型绑定到会话。新建提供方资源**不等于**悄悄修改全局默认模型。
- 为会话启用已安装、已配置的连接器；之后的实际工具调用仍遵守原有执行权限规则。
- 完全没有模型，或当前模型认证失败时，由确定性的前后端检查显示同类配置卡，不依赖失效模型诊断；保留用户的第一条任务，配置成功后只启动一次。
- 刷新或重连后恢复卡片状态；当前运行的模型或工具快照必须变化时，通过关联的后续运行接续任务。

仅提供一个 URL 不能自动把任意 REST API 变成可调用工具。新建 HTTP/SSE MCP 连接、OAuth、受控文件／环境变量导入，以及部署级代理和超时设置，可在具备专用适配器后逐项扩展。STDIO 命令、宿主执行入口、需要重启的部署设置及任意 REST API 适配需要单独评审。

### 设计边界

- Agent 只能读取**脱敏的**配置能力与状态，并创建结构化提案。只有绑定用户身份的决策接口能够批准；不给 Agent 通用写设置能力，也不能通过其他工具声称「用户已同意」。
- 密钥通过专用字段交给后端并加密保存。明文不得进入聊天消息、模型上下文、工具轨迹、SSE 事件、普通日志或浏览器持久存储。浏览器所在电脑的路径不能当成服务器路径；任何受支持的文件导入都要显示具体运行环境和读取范围。
- 如实展示资源保存范围与最终使用范围。确实支持会话级覆盖时优先只改当前会话；共享资源或全局变更必须提前说明影响。不能给只有系统级设置的项目伪造「仅本会话」选项。
- 用户确认绑定提案版本以及具体目标、差异、范围和验证计划。并发修改导致旧预览过期时应重新预览；外部探测或读取应明确告知；验证失败时保留原有效配置。
- 不能假定进行中的运行可以热切换配置快照。应在安全边界处理未完成的工具和副作用，再用经批准的新快照创建幂等的关联接续运行。用户停止或取消后不得自动接续；配置已保存与任务已继续必须分别记录。
- 「撤销本次配置」应预览反向变更并检查版本，不能覆盖之后的编辑，也不能删除仍被其他会话使用的共享资源。

### 验收标准

- [ ] 已有有效配置能够直接完成任务，不弹配置卡，也不改变原配置。
- [ ] 缺少受支持的模型 API 时，用户可在对话里补齐、确认、验证、保存并接续，无须打开设置页。
- [ ] 选用已有视觉模型时，只修改明确选择的范围；其他会话及全局默认保持不变。
- [ ] 错误凭据不会替换正常连接；修正后只应用一次。受支持的无 Key 本地端点也可使用。
- [ ] 无模型与认证失败都能进入配置流程，无须让失效模型再次诊断自己。
- [ ] 明文凭据不出现在消息、事件、日志、工具历史或模型请求中；Agent 调用不能替用户批准提案。
- [ ] 卡片显示的资源位置、生效范围、目标及可能产生费用的验证动作与后端实际行为一致。
- [ ] 拒绝或取消后不针对同一需求反复打扰；任务受阻时说明原因和可行的替代路径。
- [ ] 双击、刷新、SSE 重放、重试和服务重启至多产生一次配置应用和一个接续运行。
- [ ] 其他窗口修改配置后，旧提案标记为过期并重新预览，不覆盖新值。
- [ ] 旧运行保留历史快照；关联运行使用批准的新快照、原任务目标和已完成产物，不重放已执行的非幂等动作。
- [ ] 验证失败、保存失败和接续失败分别显示真实状态，并提供对应阶段的恢复操作。
- [ ] 停止、切换会话、归档和删除不会在错误会话应用配置，也不会重新启动已停止的任务。
- [ ] 撤销恢复原覆盖或继承关系，不覆盖后续修改，也不删除仍在使用的资源。
- [ ] 卡片支持键盘操作、可访问的错误提示、窄屏布局及中英文文案。

### 与已有工作的关系

#39 聚焦设置页中的首次连接向导；本提案增加任务上下文中的 Agent 协助配置、用户确认和任务接续。主仓当前的后端工作见 #84，其中模型与设置为 #91、对话与运行为 #89、MCP 为 #92。上述产品行为是需要实现的契约；正式开发前，具体服务归属、接口和事件方案应与当前主仓架构核对。
278.title: [Feature]: Configure settings in the conversation and resume the task

281.author: wyhohyw
281.body:
Mirrors GitCode issue [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137) (root-cause analysis: [comment](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137#comment_193508877)).

## Symptom

After deploying the stack (reported on Ubuntu 25.10, commit `c33c1ae`; the same code is on current `main`), a custom model provider cannot be configured. In **System settings → Model registry → Connect model**, the provider select shows "Custom provider", but the name / Base URL / model ID fields never appear. Only the API key, protocol, variant and "Add model" controls are visible, and picking "Custom provider" again changes nothing.

## Root cause

The backend is fine: `GET /api/providers` always returns the built-in presets. The bug is in the frontend.

1. **Presets are dropped when any unrelated settings request fails.** In `apps/web/src/App.tsx`, `modelProviderPresets` starts as `[]` and is filled only inside one `Promise.all` with ~12 other settings requests (`getMemoryGraphSettings`, `getIdeaTreeSettings`, `getSandboxNetworkSettings`, ...). There are two such batches: one at startup, one when System settings opens. If any request in a batch fails, the whole batch goes to `catch` and the preset list stays empty, even though `listProviders` itself succeeded.
2. **The select's value matches no option.** `ModelConnectWizard` starts with `selectedPresetId = "deepseek"` and `isCustom = false`. With no presets, the only `<option>` left is `custom`, but the select's `value` is still `"deepseek"`. The browser displays the first option, so the UI **shows** "Custom provider" while the component is **not** in custom mode.
3. **Re-selecting the shown option fires no change event.** `onChange` never runs, so `isCustom` stays `false`. The custom fields render only when `isCustom` is true, so they never appear. `selectedPreset` is also `undefined`, so the name and Base URL override fields under "Advanced" are hidden too.

Reproduced with a component test that renders the wizard with `presets=[]`:

```text
presets=[]              : {"selectValue":"deepseek","options":["custom"],"hasCustomUrl":false}
presets loaded, custom  : {"selectValue":"custom","options":13,"hasCustomUrl":true}
```

Which settings request fails in the reporter's environment is still unknown; we have asked on the GitCode issue.

## Proposed fix

**A. Load the provider registry on its own (`App.tsx`).** Take `listProviders()` out of both `Promise.all` batches and request it separately, so presets and configured providers no longer depend on unrelated settings requests. Triggers and error routing stay as before: a failure while System settings is open is shown in that dialog, and a startup failure follows the existing startup rule.

**B. Keep the wizard's state consistent with its options (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`).** When the selected preset is not in the list, the wizard corrects itself:
- presets available: switch to the first preset;
- no presets: enter custom mode, so the custom fields appear;
- custom mode that was entered automatically for lack of presets switches back to the first preset once presets arrive, but only if the user has not started filling the custom fields. A custom provider the user picked is kept.

**Tests:** five new cases in `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx` cover an empty preset list, presets arriving late (with and without user input), a user-picked custom provider surviving a refresh, and a selected preset disappearing. With the wizard fix removed, three of them fail; the other two guard against regressions from the fix itself. All 27 tests in the file pass, and the web package type-checks. A browser E2E for the App-level change (one settings endpoint failing while custom-provider setup still works) has not been run yet.

---

本 issue 同步自 GitCode issue [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137)（原因分析见[评论](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137#comment_193508877)）。

## 现象

部署完成后（报告环境为 Ubuntu 25.10、commit `c33c1ae`，当前 `main` 上的相关代码相同），无法配置自定义模型服务商。在 **系统设置 → 模型注册表 → 连接模型** 中，服务商下拉框显示“自定义服务商”，但名称、Base URL、模型 ID 输入框始终不出现，只能看到 API Key、基础接口、接口变种和“添加模型”。再次选择“自定义服务商”也没有反应。

## 成因

后端没有问题：`GET /api/providers` 总会返回内置的服务商预设。问题出在前端。

1. **任何一个无关的设置请求失败，预设都会丢失。** `apps/web/src/App.tsx` 中 `modelProviderPresets` 初始为 `[]`，只在一个 `Promise.all` 里和另外约 12 个设置请求（`getMemoryGraphSettings`、`getIdeaTreeSettings`、`getSandboxNetworkSettings` 等）一起加载。这样的批量请求有两处：一处在应用启动时，一处在打开系统设置时。批量中任一请求失败，整组都会进入 `catch`，即使 `listProviders` 本身成功了，预设列表也一直为空。
2. **下拉框的 value 匹配不到任何选项。** `ModelConnectWizard` 初始状态是 `selectedPresetId = "deepseek"`、`isCustom = false`。预设为空时只剩 `custom` 一个选项，但 value 仍是 `"deepseek"`。浏览器会显示第一个选项，于是界面**显示**“自定义服务商”，组件内部却**不在**自定义模式。
3. **再次选择当前显示的选项不会触发 change 事件。** `onChange` 不执行，`isCustom` 一直为 `false`。自定义字段只在 `isCustom` 为真时渲染，所以始终不出现。同时 `selectedPreset` 为 `undefined`，“高级配置”里的名称和 Base URL 覆盖字段也被隐藏。

用 `presets=[]` 渲染向导的组件测试复现了这一点，输出见上文。

报告者环境中具体是哪个设置请求失败仍待确认，已在 GitCode issue 中询问。

## 修复方案

**A. 服务商注册表单独加载（`App.tsx`）。** 把 `listProviders()` 从两处 `Promise.all` 中拿出来单独请求，预设和已配置服务商不再受无关设置请求影响。触发时机和报错去向保持不变：系统设置打开时的失败显示在设置弹窗中，启动时的失败沿用原有规则。

**B. 向导状态与选项保持一致（`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`）。** 当前选中的预设不在列表中时，向导自动修正：
- 有预设：切到第一个预设；
- 没有预设：进入自定义模式，显示自定义字段；
- 因为没有预设而自动进入的自定义模式，在预设到达后切回第一个预设，前提是用户还没开始填写自定义字段。用户主动选择的自定义服务商会保留。

**测试：** 在 `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx` 中新增 5 个用例，覆盖预设为空、预设迟到（用户是否已填写）、用户主动选的自定义在刷新后保留、选中的预设从列表消失。撤掉向导修复后其中 3 个失败，另外 2 个用于防止修复本身引入回归。该文件 27 个用例全部通过，web 包类型检查通过。App 层改动的浏览器 E2E（模拟某个设置接口失败时仍能配置自定义服务商）尚未运行。

283.body:
## Problem and intended outcome

Strengthen the existing L1–L5 gates so that core scientific features have explicit regression protection, and introduce the full, version-pinned BiomniBench-DA suite as an L5 capability non-regression gate. Keep the existing shared catalog, frozen plans, candidate-SHA/backend identity checks, and exact execution accounting.

BiomniBench-DA should measure data-analysis capability; it must not be treated as complete coverage of Idea Tree, remote execution, provenance, Reviewer, or upgrade/recovery behavior. Those features need dedicated acceptance cases.

This is a follow-up implementation plan to #248. Its pre-merge L5 certification proposal is an explicit policy extension beyond the original release-only L5 scope. Related prerequisites: #252 (wait for the complete Biomni execution/wake chain before checking delivery) and #245 (endpoint latency and empty-terminal-turn diagnostics). Reuse those investigations rather than duplicate them. The source review used commit `e9eac417f564a76a84e5e154a8d8cb9031e1f215`; counts below describe that snapshot, not newly executed CI results. Reconcile with current main before implementation. GitHub rulesets and Environment settings were not verified in this review.

## Current coverage and gaps

- L3 declares nine real cases: response, tool, files, memory, artifact, workspace, cancellation, and two Runner wait/finish recovery cases.
- L4/L5 currently select the same 19 real identities: those nine plus five DRB cases, Research Team, PUCT compression, J5 statistics, and two run/artifact-card provenance journeys. There is no eligible L5-only increment.
- Idea Tree is **not untested**: it has Python/API/package tests and a mocked browser journey covering pause/resume, three rounds, independent assessments, persistence, and termination. The browser fixture supplies one candidate per round and fixed scores; it does not establish real-model research quality or realistic multi-branch exploration.
- Existing Reviewer and literature tests already cover several evidence, identity, lifecycle, and failure contracts. Extend their missing boundaries rather than duplicate them.
- BiomniBench-DA currently has two quarantined cases using a local rubric judge adapter. Evaluation errors are recorded as non-gating, and there is no capability threshold.
- The migration ledger lists 77 Neo4j external identities and 17 unreviewed delegation identities. Map existing replacement coverage before reinstating or retiring individual cases.
- Some public-API journeys have standalone commands but are not wired into the shared CI plan.

## L5: full BiomniBench-DA capability certification

- [ ] Define a versioned manifest for the complete intended BiomniBench-DA release: task IDs, authorized data assets/checksums, instructions, evaluator/grader version, generator and judge configuration, tools, budgets, and attempts. Missing prerequisites must not silently shrink the suite.
- [ ] Repair the current isolated-task prerequisites, then expand beyond the two existing cases to the complete manifest. Record all exclusions explicitly; do not label an incomplete run as full-suite certification.
- [ ] Decide and name the evaluation protocol. The current local rubric adapter is not the upstream Gemini verifier; scores from different protocols/judges must not be silently compared or presented as equivalent official scores.
- [ ] Emit separate `delivery`, `evaluation`, and `capability` verdicts. Required evaluation errors, missing scores, non-finite values, or mismatched identities prevent certification. Optional disabled audits must be explicitly N/A.
- [ ] Define product-failure scoring up front. Generation failures, timeouts, and missing answers cannot disappear from the denominator. Infrastructure/judge failures must remain visible as blocked/incomplete certification, not be silently converted to successful results.
- [ ] Establish an approved baseline with per-task results. Freeze comparable backend/model/judge/data/grader/tool/budget identities; do not compare against an ever-moving baseline that can gradually regress.
- [ ] Calibrate a non-inferiority rule and tolerable regression margin using repeated measurements. Preserve all attempts, use a predefined repetition/review policy, and prohibit retry-until-green or best-of-unreported-attempts reporting.
- [ ] Inspect overall capability, task-category regressions, execution success rate, and severe per-task failures. Track latency, resource usage, and cost separately from answer quality.
- [ ] Bind the verdict and retained evidence to the actual candidate SHA and relevant asset hashes. Reuse certification only when the entire declared execution identity remains applicable.
- [ ] Retain dedicated acceptance cases for core features outside DA benchmark coverage, plus previous-release-to-candidate upgrade/read/continue validation where supported.

### Agreed public-50 gate and recovery policy (2026-10-20)

This is the agreed follow-up specification, not a claim that the current PR implements or has validated every requirement below. This update changes descriptions only; no code is submitted.

#### Quality decision and comparable baseline

The operator's cross-run comparison found a maximum per-task score spread of 76 points and reported 8 tasks with spreads greater than 40 points and 9 with spreads greater than 20 points. These are operator-reported diagnostic counts; the two threshold counts must not be assumed disjoint. Given the observed per-task variability, use the arithmetic mean of all **50** task scores as the quality gate. Retain individual scores and spreads for diagnosis, without hard per-task score regression thresholds.

Compare against a reviewed, frozen public-50 baseline under comparable dataset, generator/judge, evaluator, measurement, backend, machine/resource-class, concurrency and budget configurations. Cross-machine/mixed-revision diagnostic summaries are not themselves an approved baseline. All 50 tasks must have valid delivery and scores before computing a certifying mean; do not shrink the denominator, fill missing scores with zero, or claim a pass from the completed subset.

#### Warning and blocking thresholds

Let B be the approved baseline aggregate and C the current comparable aggregate. Trigger a warning or block when the stated threshold is **reached or exceeded**; a block takes precedence over a warning. Percentage increases mean (C - B) / B, with a positive baseline required.

| Metric | Aggregation across the 50 tasks | Warning | Block |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality score | Arithmetic mean, denominator fixed at 50 | B - C >= 3 score points | B - C >= 5 score points |
| Token consumption | Sum of generation + judge tokens; retain the two components separately | Increase >= 15% | Increase >= 25% |
| Tool rounds | Sum of recorded tool rounds; retain tool-call counts for diagnosis | Increase >= 30% | Increase >= 50% |
| Peak worker RSS | Maximum per-task sampled peak RSS, not a sum of task peaks | C - B >= max(20% of B, 1 GiB) | C - B >= max(30% of B, 2 GiB) |
| Research duration | Sum of per-task research durations, excluding preparation and judging | Increase >= 20% | Increase >= 30% |

Use metric-specific thresholds, not one shared resource-increase ratio. Keep absolute case timeouts, memory/cost budgets and completeness checks separate from these relative regression rules. Warnings remain visible; blocking thresholds prevent certification. These thresholds are an initial agreed policy to calibrate with comparable repeated runs, not statistically derived confidence bounds. A low but valid score or an exceeded resource threshold is not an execution/evaluation failure eligible for automatic retry-until-green.

#### Deferred, classified recovery: at most three retries

1. Finish the first pass over all 50 tasks before retrying failures. Preserve successful tasks and build a failed/incomplete-task inventory with stage, error, artifact completeness, attempt IDs and execution identity. Upstream LLM instability and stochastic inference motivate bounded recovery, but do not establish the cause of every failure.
2. **Research/delivery failure:** if `trace.md` and `answer.txt` were not both completely produced for the same completed research attempt, rerun that task end to end. Check completion evidence and artifact integrity, not just file existence or remnants from a previous attempt.
3. **Evaluation-only failure:** if both artifacts are complete and research delivery is verified, retry evaluation only against those saved, immutable artifacts. Do not regenerate the research result; retain artifact hashes and the research-attempt identity. Examples include judge timeout, invalid JSON, missing score or incomplete judge usage.
4. Allow **at most three additional retries after the initial attempt** (at most four attempts for a task in total). Use one per-task recovery counter across research and evaluation recovery, so changing failure stage or nesting a judge retry does not reset or multiply the limit. Stop at the first valid completed result; do not select the highest score. A successful research retry whose evaluation fails uses evaluation-only recovery for the remaining retry allowance.
5. If the task remains unresolved after three retries, locate and document the failing stage/root cause where evidence permits, then file or link a deduplicated tracking issue with the candidate SHA, task ID, attempt history, errors, artifacts and known/unknown resource usage. The suite remains failed/incomplete rather than silently passing. Creating those future tracking issues is an implementation requirement, not an action performed by this description update.

#### Evidence and cost accounting

Keep initial failures, every retry and recovery type, the final selected result, first-pass success rate and recovered completion rate. Publish comparable per-task result aggregates and the **actual whole-run cost including all failed and retried research/judge attempts** separately, so recovery cannot hide extra token usage or elapsed time. Include known retry usage in the cost/budget report; do not pool measurements with different accounting scopes into one comparison.

A timed-out request without reported usage remains unknown cost, never zero. Evaluation-only recovery may restore a valid score but cannot retroactively make earlier unknown usage complete or turn the attempt into a full E2E rerun. Do not certify resource non-regression while required accounting is incomplete; preserve separate delivery, evaluation, quality and resource-accounting verdicts. Resource aggregates selected for comparison must use the same declared retry-accounting scope as their approved baseline.

### Required trigger decision: merge gate versus release gate

The current L5 workflow is triggered after a version tag; that can block publication but cannot prevent a regression from entering main. The intended outcome here includes **pre-merge capability protection**.

- [ ] Make L5 certification callable for the final merge candidate (or a deliberately formed merge batch), and require its verdict before that candidate enters main. A rebuilt candidate must not reuse incompatible evidence.
- [ ] Retain release-time asset checks; reuse an earlier certification only with an explicit matching-identity policy.
- [ ] Document queue latency, concurrency, budget, and failure-localization behavior. If the chosen policy runs only on selected changes or only nightly, state the weaker guarantee explicitly rather than claiming every merge is fully benchmark-certified.

## L4: prioritized real scientific journeys

Priority applies to the **new L4 coverage**, not to removal of existing tests. P0 is the first implementation tranche; P1 follows once completeness and budget controls are available.

| Priority | Feature / proposed case | Observable acceptance criteria |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | **Idea Tree: multi-branch, multi-round research with an independently computable evaluator** | Generate distinct candidates; reject hard-constraint violations; execute candidates where applicable; preserve lineage; propagate prior insights into later rounds; select a valid result using independent evidence. Do not require every exploratory round to improve monotonically. |
| **P0** | **Reviewer: paired correct and deliberately flawed reports** | Detect unsupported citations, numeric/unit errors, and evidence from the wrong run/version; avoid false accusations on correct reports; return inconclusive when evidence is insufficient. Measure false positives as well as missed defects. |
| **P0** | **Scientific calculation / J5: fixed-data analysis with an independent numerical oracle** | Persist reproducible computation and verify report values, units, and evidence against independently calculated expectations, rather than merely requiring a Markdown artifact. |
| **P1** | **Literature research: retrieval → acquisition → extraction → citation → report** | Verify source identity and evidence support; exercise representative live connector/PDF paths with bounded budgets. Keep deterministic source/failure fixtures in L2 and distinguish provider availability from product defects. |
| **P1** | **Multi-agent research: successful, failed, and delayed child tasks** | Preserve task/result identity; surface partial failure; propagate cancellation; avoid duplicate dispatch and missing results; prevent an unsupported “all succeeded” final conclusion. Extend existing Research Team coverage. |
| **P1** | **Evolve/PUCT: independently evaluated candidate optimization** | Verify candidate/parent/baseline identity, legitimate selection, and validation/test separation; invalid or failed evaluations cannot win. Keep seed-as-best valid; do not require arbitrary improvement in every run. |

For all cases, enter through the product's public interfaces, record model/backend identity and usage, enforce explicit execution budgets, and retain auditable evidence. Generating a score is not itself a passing capability verdict.

## L1–L3: close engineering and integration gaps

### L1: trustworthy policy and manifests

- [ ] Add independent validation of CI-sensitive changes against a trusted base. A change must not weaken selectors/gates and their self-tests together without detection; legitimate policy changes need an explicit review path. Unknown impact must fail or fall back to the full intended plan.
- [ ] Validate benchmark manifest schema, unique IDs, frozen inputs, required evaluation fields, and explicit exclusions.
- [ ] Restore appropriate dependency-vulnerability, secret, and static-security checks that are not replaced by the current test gate.
- [ ] Verify repository administration separately: required `merge-gate`, Merge Queue, current-head review/stale-approval dismissal, and permitted Environment refs. YAML presence is not proof that these are enforced.

### L2: deterministic product and scientific contracts

- [ ] Register suitable existing public-API journeys in the shared catalog, especially remote execution wake-up, detached Runner behavior, and memory/provenance journeys. Preserve isolated processes/data and planned/executed accounting.
- [ ] Add a reproducible temporary Neo4j integration job for the applicable external identities; local-backend tests are not a substitute for Neo4j behavior.
- [ ] Map the 17 unreviewed delegation identities to current Swarm coverage; restore missing behaviors or explicitly document verified replacements.
- [ ] Extend Idea Tree mocked E2E to multiple branches with good, weak, and invalid candidates, pruning, failure recovery, and final selection assertions.
- [ ] Test evaluation aggregation with injected judge timeouts, missing/invalid scores, wrong versions, and missing tasks. No incomplete evaluation may produce full certification.
- [ ] Test suite request/token budget enforcement, including retries, children, judges, cancellation, and unknown usage. Existing context or feature-local budgets do not establish a suite-wide cost ceiling.
- [ ] Extend literature/Reviewer fixtures with wrong pages, unsupported citations, unit errors, cross-session/version evidence, and correct counterexamples. Consider sanitized HTTP replay with CI auto-recording disabled; keep online freshness checks separate.
- [ ] Verify remote success and recovery: input transfer, execution in separate storage, artifact return, completion wake-up, no duplicate execution after reconnect, and no orphan work after cancellation.
- [ ] Verify full provenance from input version through code/environment/execution to report; same-named files in different sessions must not mix, and old reports must not silently point to new versions.
- [ ] Audit existing process-recovery tests and add missing actual API/Runner/Swarm restart journeys. Browser refresh and session reopening do not establish server recovery.

### L3: small real-model and distribution acceptance

- [ ] Add a bounded real-model smoke for critical feature entry points such as Idea Tree; leave deep research and quality evaluation to L4/L5.
- [ ] Exercise critical upload → execution → artifact-read behavior against the actual distribution candidate. Preserve the existing two-architecture binary and Docker gates and publish the assets that were tested.
- [ ] Apply explicit paid-call budgets to the merge-candidate suite without weakening identity or failure accounting.

## Follow-up coverage audits

- [ ] Define supported-platform obligations before adding macOS, real SSH, NPU, R, or additional dependency matrices. Do not infer coverage from Linux/amd64 tests or arm64 boot smoke.
- [ ] Audit long-running concurrency, process cleanup, and upgrade/migration tests before adding duplicates.
- [ ] Maintain a feature × tier × failure-mode coverage map linked to case IDs, so “has unit tests” is not mistaken for “has real scientific acceptance.”
- [ ] Add deduplicated nightly failure tracking, ownership, recovery handling, and sufficient release-evidence retention.

## Completion criteria and rollout

1. Make results trustworthy first: frozen manifests, evaluation-completeness contracts, budget controls, baseline protocol, and required-check configuration.
2. Bring suitable existing journeys and external integration tests into routine CI; resolve delegation coverage mapping.
3. Land L4 P0 cases, then P1 enhancements, reusing existing fixtures and assertions where appropriate.
4. Enable full L5 certification on the intended pre-merge candidate, with calibrated non-regression rules and artifact-bound release evidence.

Acceptance must include deliberate fault injection: a missing selected task, judge failure, invalid winning candidate, mismatched fingerprint, exceeded budget, or weakened selection policy must not produce a green certification. Selection-only checks are not evidence that the complete suite executed successfully.
