284.author: ink999107
284.body:
## Environment

- Release package `sciencediscovery` **0.3.0-beta** (x86_64), started with `ScienceDiscovery serve`, Linux

## Symptom

Soon after startup the right-side task panel in the web UI shows `invalid internal token`, and the **Retry** button never recovers — the same error returns every time. Chat and agent runs work normally.

## What the shipped package does

1. The payload contains no evolve sidecar, and the launcher neither starts one nor passes `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` / `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to the API (confirmed in the running API process' environment). Memory-graph gets the opposite treatment — the launcher seeds it with a per-run random token (`services/launcher/src/memory-graph.ts:27`).
2. With both variables unset the API falls back to `http://127.0.0.1:4313` with the constant token `sciencediscovery-evolve-local` (`services/api/src/bootstrap/config.ts:253-256`).
3. Whatever process happens to hold `127.0.0.1:4313` therefore receives the API's evolve traffic. In my case that port was held by another process running an evolve sidecar configured with its own token, so the calls came back `401 {"detail":"invalid internal token"}` — and the frontend relayed that raw `detail` string into the task panel, where Retry just re-issues the same call.

I verified the error did not come from my own stack's memory-graph: the launcher-generated token matches the API's on both sides, and its access log shows zero 401s. The string is in fact the loopback-auth rejection detail shared by both sidecars (`services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/auth.py:40`, `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/auth.py:40`) — which is why it reaches users with no hint of which service or token failed.

## Why the fallback itself is the problem

- The API ends up calling an arbitrary process that happens to bind a fixed port, authenticating with a token guessable from the public source. A sidecar that rejects it produces the unrecoverable raw error above; a process that accepts it (or runs an evolve sidecar with the token unset — auth is permissive then) would be silently used by this installation.
- Run specifications sent to the sidecar carry the LLM proxy URL and token (`llm`, `judge` fields in `services/api/src/evolution/sidecar.ts`), so whatever holds the port also receives those credentials.

## Suggestions

- Give evolve the same launcher treatment as memory-graph: start it from the payload with a per-run random token, or explicitly disable it / point the API at an operator-configured URL, so the constant fallback is never reached.
- When a sidecar call fails, report which sidecar failed instead of relaying the raw `detail` to the UI.
- Prefer per-installation fallback credentials over source constants, and avoid fixed default sidecar ports (related: #267).

Workaround I applied locally: launch with `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_URL` pointing at an unused loopback port, so the API no longer calls whatever holds 4313.
284.title: Hardcoded evolve sidecar fallback (127.0.0.1:4313 + fixed token) surfaces raw "invalid internal token" in the UI

286.author: zhaozhaozz
286.body:
Nightly real E2E skips J5 while the managed Python base is still in its normal install phase. The gate then counts that skip as a failed shard.

## What happened

Scheduled Nightly run [38318935663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38318935663) (main `b0a25b4c555fe75c9a44ddd942817600f6821510`, 2026-10-13) failed job Gate / Real E2E (research-9). The only identity in that shard is:

`playwright:test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` — `J5 真实请求生成统计结果并交付 Markdown`

The skip reason was:

`BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (installing: Creating the managed Python base environment)`

The real-model credentials were present. The same night, the other real cases passed except research-10, which failed for a separate delivery-budget reason. J5 itself passed on the 2026-10-09 dispatch (37875334064), both 2026-10-10 runs (38041373183 and 38081832760), and the 2026-10-11 schedule (38170922621).

## Why the skip is a race

`Creating the managed Python base environment` is the normal `creating-python-base` phase while the runner installs the managed Python base (Python 3.12 plus the pinned scientific packages). The HTTP server is already accepting requests, so `GET /health` succeeds and `GET /api/environment-setup` returns `state=installing` until that install finishes. The GET does not start the install and does not wait for it.

J5 observed that status once and called `testInfo.skip` whenever `state` was not `ready`. Real E2E requires every planned identity to execute, so a skip fails the shard (`SHARD_FAILED`, and the identity is `NOT_RUN`).

Mocked journeys keep an immediate readiness assertion. Only this real journey should wait, and a `failed` install or a deadline that still shows `installing` must stay BLOCKED.

## Expected

J5 polls the existing setup status for a bounded cold-start window, continues when the state becomes `ready`, and still reports BLOCKED if setup fails or is not ready when the deadline passes.

290.author: wyhohyw
290.body:
Startup and opening System settings still load most of their data with `Promise.all`. One rejected request discards every sibling that already succeeded, so a single unhealthy endpoint blanks unrelated panels. #281 / #288 pulled `client.listProviders()` out of both batches, which restored custom-provider setup. The same coupling remains for every other call in those batches.

## What still fails together

Both sites are in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.

Opening System settings loads, as one batch: `listModels`, `listConnectors`, `listSkills`, `listSkillLibraries`, `getGlobalSettings`, `getTimeoutSettings`, `getQuotaSettings`, `getSandboxNetworkSettings`, `getWebSettings`, `getMemoryGraphSettings`, `getIdeaTreeSettings`.

Startup loads, as one batch: `listProjects`, `listModels`, `getModelCatalog`, `listConnectors`, `listSkills`, `listSkillLibraries`, `getGlobalSettings`, `getTimeoutSettings`, `getQuotaSettings`, `getSandboxNetworkSettings`, `getProxySettings`, `getMcpProxyPolicies`, `listMcpSources`, `getWebSettings`, `getMemoryGraphSettings`, `getIdeaTreeSettings`.

`Promise.all` keeps the first rejection and throws away the fulfilled values. A `GET /api/memory/settings` 500 therefore leaves models, the global default, connectors, skills, timeouts, quotas, and the other panels at their initial empty state, even when those requests returned 200. The provider rows can still appear, because that read is already independent, while the registry shows "已添加 0/N" and a default-model select of only "未配置" for models that exist on the server.

A successful empty list and a failed read must stay different. After a failure the UI should show that read's error, and should not present the missing data as a confirmed empty configuration.

## Suggested change

Settle each call on its own in both effects. Apply each success to its own state. Report each failure through the existing path (`reportSystemSettingsError` while System settings is the operation in progress, otherwise the page error). Keep `listProviders()` as #288 left it. `setProjectsLoaded(true)` on the startup path must still run after the project list settles, whether or not the other reads fail.

## Out of scope

Saving the global default model from an in-memory `globalSettings` that was never loaded, and `replaceGlobalSettings` then replacing the whole stored object, is a separate save-path bug. Isolating the reads does not fix that write. Track it on its own.

## Acceptance

- With one endpoint in either batch forced to 500, every sibling that returned 200 is still applied, at startup and again when System settings opens. The two paths are checked separately.
- The failed read is still visible as an error.
- An endpoint that succeeds with an empty body still shows the real empty state.
- An instance that already has a model and a global default still shows that model and that default when an unrelated settings endpoint fails.

Related: #281, #288. Reported on the GitCode mirror as https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137.
290.title: One failing settings request discards the other startup and System settings results

291.body:
Follow-up to merged #288. Suggested priority: **P1**, because a successful model-connection action can silently delete persisted global overrides.

The issue remains in `main` at `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310`. The integration reproduction below ran against the final PR frontend (`cb9fe1f5`) with the real API/store and a local stub model endpoint; the affected `App.tsx` code is unchanged in the merge.

## Reproduction and observed result

1. Use an isolated instance with **no registered models**.
2. Persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
3. Make browser `GET /api/memory/settings` requests return HTTP 500, starting before page load and continuing while System settings is open. Keep `GET /api/settings`, provider/model APIs, and model connection testing healthy.
4. Open System settings → Models, enter a custom provider backed by a working model endpoint, and click “保存并连接”.
5. The UI reports “模型已连接”. Inspect the browser's `PUT /api/settings` and read back persisted overrides.

**Actual write and persisted result** (generated ID abbreviated):

```json
{ "modelId": "<new-model-id>" }
```

All three pre-existing override keys have disappeared. Reloading cannot restore them.

**Expected:** only `modelId` changes; the connector, semantic-review, reasoning-effort, and any other unrelated overrides remain intact.

Control runs with the same initial overrides and real App/API:
- All reads healthy: connection succeeds and all overrides are preserved.
- Only `GET /api/providers` fails: custom connection succeeds and all overrides are preserved.
- Only `GET /api/memory/settings` fails: connection succeeds but all existing overrides are lost.

## Cause across the repository

- The startup and System-settings effects still batch `getGlobalSettings()` with unrelated requests. A sibling rejection prevents `setGlobalSettings` from running even when `GET /api/settings` returned 200. This read-path problem is already tracked by #290.
- The shared default-model callback in [App.tsx:5044–5052](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310/apps/web/src/App.tsx#L5044-L5052) spreads `globalSettings?.overrides ?? {}`, then calls `replaceGlobalSettings`. It treats “not loaded” as an authoritative empty configuration.
- [ModelConnectWizard.tsx:359–367](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L359-L367) does obtain a fresh settings snapshot, but keeps it locally for rollback. Its [first-model callback](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L416-L422) passes only the model ID, so that snapshot does not protect the App write.
- [Store.replaceGlobalSettings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310/services/api/src/store.ts#L2215-L2222) intentionally replaces the full override object; it does not merge omitted keys.

The unsafe callback predates #288. The restored custom-provider flow exposes its impact during degraded startup. This issue owns the **save-path data loss**; #290 owns independent loading and accurate UI state. Fixing read isolation alone does not make a write safe when the global-settings read itself fails.

## Test gap and acceptance

The degraded-settings E2E currently [asserts connection success and provider existence](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310/test/journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings.spec.ts#L181-L194), but does not seed non-model overrides and verify they survive. Wizard unit tests mock `onDefaultModelSet`, so they do not exercise the destructive parent callback.

- [ ] Add an integration/E2E regression using the real App callback and persistence layer: seed zero models plus non-empty global overrides, inject the unrelated 500, connect the first model, and assert both the new default and every existing override in a subsequent API read.
- [ ] Preserve unrelated fields when setting or clearing a default through the registry's shared callback as well.
- [ ] If an authoritative settings snapshot cannot be obtained, report the failure without replacing stored settings from an assumed `{}`. Include a regression where `GET /api/settings` itself fails.
- [ ] Cover wizard fallback/rollback paths so an unavailable initial snapshot cannot clear existing settings either.
- [ ] Retain the successful custom-provider behavior from #288, including unavailable presets and user-entered custom fields.

Use a fresh isolated data directory and a local stub model endpoint for these tests; do not rely only on success banners or a mocked default-model callback.

292.body:
TC-E2E-01's delivery checker rejects numbered Markdown section headings even when the report contains all three requested sections. The prompt, managed extension, and checker should agree on optional section numbering so a valid report does not trigger a formatting-only rewrite.

## Reproduction

Pass this report to `checkDeliverable` in `test/fixtures/deliverable-check.mjs`:

```markdown
## 3. Methods
## 4. Results
## 9. References
```

Current result: `ok: false`, with `missing: ["Methods", "Results", "References"]`. Expected: `ok: true`.

The checker extracts ATX headings outside fenced code blocks, then compares each entire lowercased title to the required name. It compares `3. methods` to `methods` and therefore rejects the numbered section. The user prompt requests the three section names without excluding numbering, while the report-writer's default template uses numbered headings when formatting is unspecified.

## Observed impact

In Nightly [38318935663](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38318935663), research-10's `deliverable_check` reported all three sections missing at `03:53:39Z` even though the report used the numbered headings above. A further report-writer task was dispatched at `03:55:57Z` and cancelled at `03:57:06Z`; total generation was 3,308,937 ms against the 3,300,000 ms budget. The prior report-writing task took about 516 seconds, so the remaining time could not accommodate another similar rewrite.

This does not establish that heading normalization alone makes every full research run finish within its budget. A successful longer research path in Nightly [38170922621](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38170922621) completed delivery in 50.2 minutes. The requested change preserves the existing 55-minute CI budget and 60-minute local default.

## Acceptance

- Count only ATX headings outside fenced code blocks.
- Accept both `## Methods` and `## 3. Methods`, likewise Results and References.
- Remove at most one leading section number matching `^\d+(?:\.\d+)*[.)]?\s+`, then require an exact, case-insensitive section-name match. Preserve trailing `#` stripping.
- Reject `## Methods and materials`, `## 3. Methodology`, prose mentions, and fenced-code examples.
- Apply the same rule in the user prompt, managed extension, MCP tool description, and checker. Have the coordinator pass the rule verbatim in the report-writer's Format Expectation instead of falling back to the default seven-section template.
- Add unit coverage, including the three numbered headings from the failed report; preserve existing negative cases.

This is separate from #239, which tracks how a still-running run is classified when its budget expires. Do not close that issue or change timeout classification in this fix. The report-writer's default template and both generation-budget values are outside scope.

Follow-up discovered during the repository-wide review of #295; related to #288 and #291. Suggested priority: **P2**.

A failed model connection can silently undo a successful settings change made by another tab or API client while the connection test is running. The wizard restores the entire global-settings snapshot captured before the attempt, including fields it did not change.

This is **pre-existing**, not a regression introduced by #295. The same browser/API reproduction failed on both the base commit `4f8af1b9ebe491763a787a863e0b004cb11a6310` and PR revision `45366a904edc7c57e69d36ce79b944e75b382d45`. The rollback code remains unchanged in the latest PR revision `d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635`.

## Reproduction

Use an isolated instance, the real API/store, and a local model endpoint that returns an authentication failure. No real provider credentials are needed.

1. Start with no registered models and persist these global overrides through `PUT /api/settings`:
   ```json
   {
     "enabledConnectorIds": [],
     "semanticReviewEnabled": true,
     "thinkingEffort": "high"
   }
   ```
2. Open System settings → Models and connect a custom provider. Let the wizard successfully read global settings, create the provider, and register its first model. The backend automatically selects this first model as the global default.
3. While `POST /api/models/:id/test` is pending, use a second API client to read the current overrides and successfully write them back with only `thinkingEffort` changed to `"low"`. Preserve the current temporary `modelId` in this write.
4. Let the connection test return an authentication failure.
5. Read back `GET /api/settings`.

Observed interleaving, with the generated model ID abbreviated:

| Stage | Persisted overrides |
| --- | --- |
| Initial state / wizard snapshot | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |
| Successful concurrent write | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"low","modelId":"temporary-model"}` |
| Wizard rollback | `{"enabledConnectorIds":[],"semanticReviewEnabled":true,"thinkingEffort":"high"}` |

**Actual:** the concurrent `"low"` setting is silently replaced by the old `"high"` value.

**Expected:** undo only this attempt's default-model change when it is still owned by the attempt; preserve the other client's `"low"` setting and every other unrelated override.

The browser reproduction intercepts the model-test request only to schedule a second, successful write through the real settings API before allowing the failing model test to proceed. It uses the actual App, wizard, HTTP API, and store.

## Cause and implementation boundary

[`ModelConnectWizard.restoreSavedOverrides`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/apps/web/src/ModelConnectWizard.tsx#L360-L377) calls `replaceGlobalSettings(savedOverrides)` on failure. This replaces the whole settings object with a snapshot taken before provider creation and model testing.

The backend needs the attempt's automatic default cleared before it can delete the temporary model, but restoring unrelated fields is unnecessary. The same unconditional rollback also runs when existing models meant the attempt did not change the default.

The [documented settings boundary](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/d46a9887ce61c0558d62769be4941cf8c3195635/docs/en/developer-docs/plugins.md#L220-L232) already provides a catalog-level settings mutex and revision-checked plugin writes. Classic PUT intentionally remains last-writer-wins. This issue concerns the wizard's stale whole-object compensation; it does not require changing all classic PUT semantics.

A frontend-only fresh GET followed by another whole-object PUT still leaves a read/write race. Use an atomic conditional undo or equivalent version/ownership check at the existing server-side settings boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed connection preserves unrelated global-setting changes committed while that connection is in progress, including explicit empty connector selections.
- [ ] Rollback changes `modelId` only if the current default still belongs to this attempt; a newer default chosen by another writer is not overwritten.
- [ ] If the attempt never changed the global default, cleanup does not restore the old global-settings snapshot.
- [ ] In the uncontended first-model failure case, the temporary automatic default is safely undone and only the attempt's provider/models are deleted; existing references remain protected.
- [ ] Add a deterministic integration regression test using real settings persistence and an interleaved second writer. Check persisted settings after rollback and reopening the store, rather than only asserting mock delete calls.
- [ ] Cover both an unrelated-field edit and a concurrent default-model change, while retaining #295's test that a failed initial settings read creates no provider/model.

This is separate from #291: here the wizard's initial settings read succeeds, and the loss occurs during later failure rollback after another writer has saved successfully.
298.title: [Bug]: Model connection rollback overwrites concurrent global settings changes

## Environment

## Symptom

On the left-side project panel, the **collapse** control has no effect: clicking it does not hide the projects listed below, and the panel's expanded/collapsed state does not change.

## Repro

1. Open the web UI.
2. Look at the left-side project panel.
3. Click its collapse control.
4. Expected: the list of projects under the panel is hidden / the panel folds.
5. Actual: the list stays visible, no state change.

## Note

The same UI has working collapse/expand controls for other sections — `memory.action.collapseAll` / `expandAll`, `mcp.collapseServer` / `expandServer`, `artifact.collapseRunOutputs` / `expandRunOutputs`, and the file/skill sidebars (`收起包文件侧栏`, `收起 Skill 侧栏`). Only the project panel's toggle appears not to apply its state. Comparing its click handler / state binding to those working sidebars should make the difference easy to find.
